note: Goal statements and targets are AUTHORED — a commitment cannot be derived. Every current value is MEASURED by hq/server.py's evaluator. A goal nothing can measure says so and counts against this pillar's assurance fraction.

verdict_template.unassured: Nothing is failing; we are still building checks for {unassured} of the {total} areas, and the plans for those are written.
verdict_template.ok: Green on main, and the test runs are recent enough to believe.

goals.why_it_matters: Recorded games are the training data phase 4 runs on. A break here is silent until bot training fails, which is the worst possible time to find out.

measure.label: the rules that keep a replay reproducible, and whether the recorded games still replay

members.label: no raw randomness outside the two sanctioned generators
the sim layer touches no node, autoload or input
one gateway for every world change
recorded games that can still be tied to the build that made them

path_to_green.narrative: Run `python3 tools/check_gateway.py` — a broken rule names the line that broke it, and what the line should have done instead.

action.label: Put it on the VP of Engineering's list
action.title: Repair the rule that keeps recorded games replayable
action.ask: One of the four checks behind this goal is failing, so a recorded game may no longer replay to the same ending — and recorded games are the training data the robots will learn from. Find the change that broke the rule and put the rule back, rather than relaxing it.
action.first_action: Run python3 tools/check_gateway.py and the unit suite, and read which of the four checks is failing.

goals.statement_short: The build fails either because the code does not compile or because one of its tests failed.

path_to_green.narrative: The run that failed identifies the job that broke it, and that job's log shows the test or the compile error underneath. Open the run, fix what it shows, and push the fix to main.

action.label: Put the failed build on Engineering's list
action.title: Restore the failed build on main
action.ask: The newest finished tests workflow on main failed. Open the failing run, identify the first failed check, repair the cause rather than weakening the check, and push the verified fix to main.
action.first_action: Open the failing run linked on the Engineering page and read the first failed job's log. Reproduce that exact command from a clean checkout before changing code.

goals.statement_short: pushing a version tag ships the build, but the store page still waits on you to paste it
goals.why_it_matters: Shipping should happen on its own when the conditions hold, rather than being a ritual you perform. Your judgement belongs in the standing policy — ship whenever these things are true — and the pipeline should carry it from there, all the way to players. Every step that still waits on a person is a step that will be forgotten, delayed, or done at midnight.

measure.label: what pushing a version tag does on its own, from the build to the store page a player lands on

members.label: pushing a v-tag uploads the build to itch.io with no hand on it (butler push, in .github/workflows/release.yml)
the same workflow also publishes the store page text from ITCH_PAGE.md

path_to_green.narrative: The build half is done. The store page half has no sanctioned route: itch.io publishes no API for page text — butler, the upload tool itch.io gives you, has 47 commands and every one of them moves build files, and the serverside API can only read — so the dashboard's editor is the only way in. That makes this a call for you: keep the paste as a permanent step in the runbook, or have the workflow drive itch.io's editor in a headless browser. [The card](#/inbox/Q-111) lays out both.
